# End-to-end update proof

`TestUpdateAptE2E` (set `PKGFORMAT_E2E=1`; needs podman and a local Debian image
with apt, default `localhost/debtools:bookworm`, override with
`PKGFORMAT_E2E_IMAGE`) publishes a repository with this module's writers in
two generations and lets the real `apt-get update` in a container fetch it from
a loopback HTTP server, keeping `/var/lib/apt/lists` between runs. It checks,
from the server's access log and from the lists apt ends up with, that apt:

- accepted the signed `InRelease` (`signed-by=` a key file);
- fetched `Packages`, `Translation-en` and `Contents` by hash;
- on the second generation read `Packages.diff/Index` by hash, applied a single
  patch and did not download the whole `Packages.xz`;
- ended with files byte-identical to the ones published.

The same repository is then updated with `apt.Update` and the lists compared
(`TestUpdateEndToEnd` runs the in-process half without a container).

`apt-update.sh` is the script run in the container. The Contents target is
defined on the command line the way the apt-file package configures it, since
apt does not ship one. apt only fetches an index family when the Release lists
the uncompressed form of it, so the repository lists `Translation-en` and
`Contents-amd64` plain as well as compressed, as `apt-ftparchive` does.

Verified with apt 2.6.2 (Debian bookworm). Nothing here is recorded data: the
repository is generated by the test.
